intent: Approve a commit without a change check when only wording changed.

edit.summary:
I changed `SKILL.md` so a commit can be approved without a passing change check when only wording changed. I didn't edit `EXAMPLES.md` and haven't run anything.

- **Commit object:** I added an optional boolean `wording_only`.
- **`approve_commit`:** It now takes an optional `wording_only` param and stores it on the commit. I also added a sentence about this to its description.
- **`checks-pass` precondition:** It now reads `target.checks_passed == true or params.wording_only == true`.
- **`approved-only-if-checked` precondition and `approved-commits-passed-their-checks` invariant:** Both now also accept `target.wording_only == true`. Without this they would have contradicted the relaxed approval rule.

The owner declares `wording_only` when approving, and nothing in the spec verifies that the change really is wording only. I did this because the request named no other mechanism.

findings.problem: The wording-only bypass rests on a flag the approver sets on the approve_commit call itself (params.wording_only). Nothing checks that the commit's change is actually wording only, such as a diff classification or the change check. Any approver can skip the change check on any commit by passing true. This removes the guarantee that a change is checked before approval. The record_approval precondition and the invariant then accept the same self-asserted value (target.wording_only), so they no longer guard anything.
findings.where: SKILL.md, Authoring, approve_commit params and effects, precondition checks-pass, and the record_approval precondition approved-only-if-checked

findings.problem: The invariant approved-commits-passed-their-checks is now false by its own name. Approved commits may never have been checked, and the check is satisfied by an unverified flag. The reason on the check_commit precondition not-approved still says 'An approved commit passed its check', which no longer holds. The glossary says the change check is what a commit runs 'before approval', and the Purpose announcement says 'Every change shows what it breaks before anything is deployed'. Both now overstate what happens.
findings.where: SKILL.md, Authoring: invariant approved-commits-passed-their-checks, precondition check_commit not-approved, Glossary 'change check', Purpose announcement

findings.problem: approve_commit sets target.wording_only = params.wording_only whenever it runs. A call that omits the optional param can overwrite or clear a wording_only value already on the commit. The precondition reads params.wording_only, while the later record_approval precondition and the invariant read target.wording_only. The two sources can disagree, for example if the flag is set on the target some other way, and the approver's claim is never reconciled with the stored value.
findings.where: SKILL.md, Authoring, approve_commit effects vs. preconditions checks-pass and approved-only-if-checked

findings.problem: Commit.wording_only has no check_commit or record_check path, and the existing Element.wording_only is set at propose time. The new Commit flag has the same name but a different origin and trust level. No example covers the new wording-only approval path, and the existing example 'approve-only-after-a-passing-check' no longer states the whole rule, since a wording-only approval now bypasses that check. The kernel's own `approve_commit` call may also still refuse an unchecked commit, so the declared bypass may not work or may fail only at the kernel.
